question.text: What does 'interoperability' mean in the context of KYC Registration Agencies (KRAs) under SEBI KRA Regulations, 2011?

answer.text: The ability of KRAs to share client trading data with stock exchanges
The ability of a KRA to determine whether the KYC documents of a client are in the custody of another KRA
The ability of KRAs to process transactions on behalf of intermediaries
The ability of KRAs to issue trading permissions to clients

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI KRA framework defines interoperability as the ability of a KRA to determine whether the KYC documents of the client are in the custody of another KRA. This enables a subsequent intermediary to access the existing KYC record rather than asking the client to redo KYC, preventing duplication and supporting seamless onboarding. The Trap: Option A sounds plausible but KRAs deal with KYC documents, not client trading data; trading data is handled by exchanges and depositories. Options C and D describe roles that do not belong to a KRA. Note: Page 183 (footnote) of the NISM Series III-A workbook defines interoperability as the KRA's ability to determine whether client KYC documents are in another KRA's custody; pages 185 and 188 support subsequent intermediary access and the prevention of KYC duplication.
